data.narrative:
Outrider operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at the Series D stage, having raised $262M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Divergent, Exotec, Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics), alongside a broader comparison universe that includes eight private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Two valuation methods triangulate on Outrider's fair value. The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement to the $262M raised proxy, implying $393M. The Peer-Median method benchmarks against five robotics companies at Series C–E stages, where the median valuation is $1.6B (range: $1.0B–$2.3B), reflecting recent funding activity in the sector. Notable peers include Exotec at $2.0B and Hadrian at $1.6B, both at Series D.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $334M (low) to $1.8B (high), with a median of $996M. The wide range reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation multiples in an active but volatile sector. Key variables include competitive positioning relative to Exotec and Hadrian, customer concentration, and near-term cash burn relative to runway. The peer-median approach anchors higher than stage-progression, suggesting either frontier-sector growth premium pricing or potential overvaluation in the peer set. Further diligence on unit economics and contract backlog would narrow this range.
